title: add a wave-start-finding fixture to the CLI render flag so a held-on-finding view renders without an overlay test

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`-render-fixture` (adj 542) lets a UI pass render CLI views without an overlay test, but no fixture shows a wave start that holds an item on a Check finding. S563 made `ork wave start` print `held: ITEM: LINE` for an item the spec check holds on a Check finding, and keep that item out of the start set (`internal/cli/wave.go:616-618`, `internal/cli/wave.go:755-757`). The only wave fixture, `wave-start`, stops before the spec check (`internal/cli/render_test.go:184-215`). So the UI pass for S563 wrote `cli_render_overlay_test.go` to get this view.

This slice adds a `wave-start-finding` fixture: a `wave start` with `--yes` where one item is held on a Check finding and another is ready and started. It is written as `wave-start-finding.txt` and listed in the UI pass brief and the docs.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/render_test.go:62` (the `renderViews` entry), `internal/cli/render_test.go:182-215` (`renderWaveStart`, shared plan and app setup), `internal/cli/render_test.go:388` (`renderFixtureNames`) and `internal/cli/render_test.go:490-493` (a new named test beside `TestRenderWaveStartFixture`)
- `internal/engine/brief.go:233` (the fixture list in the UI brief's CLI text renders section)
- `internal/engine/brief_test.go:1086-1102` (`TestUIPassBriefNamesRenderFixtures`)
- `docs/guide.md:1004-1008` (fixture list)
- `docs/design.md:829-833` (fixture list)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestRenderCLIViewsWritesFiles in `internal/cli/render_test.go`: loops over `renderFixtureNames`, so with `wave-start-finding` added to that list its subtest runs `-renders DIR -render-fixture wave-start-finding` and must find exactly `wave-start-finding.txt`, non-empty, with no ANSI escapes. Red before the change: no fixture has that name, so the run fails with `no render fixture "wave-start-finding"`.
- TestRenderWaveStartFindingFixture in `internal/cli/render_test.go` (new): `assertRenderLine(t, "wave-start-finding", ...)` finds the held line of the held item, `held: S501: Check entry "q quit": first word "q" is not a runnable command`. The implementer confirms the literal from the rendered view and may adjust it. The test also asserts that the view lists S502 as started and has no `Start this wave?` prompt. Red before the change: the fixture does not exist.
- TestUIPassBriefNamesRenderFixtures in `internal/engine/brief_test.go`: the UI brief's fixture list now ends `..., projects-setup, fake-reply and wave-start-finding`, and the other asserted texts stay. Red before the change: the brief lacks the name.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add `"wave-start-finding"` to `renderFixtureNames` in `internal/cli/render_test.go`. Write `TestRenderWaveStartFindingFixture` and the brief_test change, and see each fail.
2. In `internal/cli/render_test.go`, split `renderWaveStart` so its plan builder and fake-daemon `App` are shared with the new fixture, and `renderWaveStart` prints the same view as now. The new `renderWaveStartFinding` runs `wave start ork S501 S502 --well-specified yes --split no --yes` through `renderSteps`. It uses a `specStub` whose `spec.check` reply holds S501 with `"ready":false` and one finding (the `q quit` entry) and gives S502 `"ready":true`. Its `wave.start` reply starts only S502, with a run record so the view shows the started line. Fail the fixture if `wave.start` is asked to start S501.
3. Add the view to `renderViews()` as `{name: "wave-start-finding", text: renderWaveStartFinding}` after `wave-start`. It is not `general`, so `-renders` alone still writes the five default files.
4. Write the literal line of `TestRenderWaveStartFindingFixture` from the rendered view, as S499 did for the other fixtures.
5. In `internal/engine/brief.go:233`, change the list to `... projects-setup, fake-reply and wave-start-finding`. Update `internal/engine/brief_test.go` to match.
6. In `docs/guide.md` and `docs/design.md`, add `wave-start-finding` to the fixture list, with a few words on what it shows: a wave start with `--yes` that holds one item on a Check finding and starts the other.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- `-renders DIR -render-fixture wave-start-finding` writes wave-start-finding.txt, a wave start with --yes that prints a held: ITEM: LINE line for an item held on a Check finding, and starts the other item.
- `-renders` alone still writes only the five default files.
- The UI pass brief and the docs list wave-start-finding.

Commands:
- `go test -run TestRenderCLIViewsWritesFiles ./internal/cli` exits 0, and its wave-start-finding subtest passes.
- `go test -run TestRenderWaveStartFindingFixture ./internal/cli` exits 0.
- `go test -run TestRenderWaveStartFixture ./internal/cli` exits 0 (the existing fixture is unchanged).
- `go test -run TestUIPassBriefNamesRenderFixtures ./internal/engine` exits 0.
- `go test ./...` exits 0.
- `go vet ./...` exits 0.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
